children: TFP Group filed an F-1 registration statement for an initial public offering on the NYSE under the proposed ticker “TFP.” The Bermuda-incorporated, U.K.-tax resident company operates as the world’s largest independent managing general agent (MGA) focused on specialty (re)insurance. The company plans to use IPO proceeds primarily to repay debt under its new term loan facility and for general corporate purposes.

TFP Group is a fee‑based managing general underwriter and risk allocator focused on specialty (re)insurance. The company operates two complementary segments: Fidelis Underwriting, which originates and allocates complex risks across Specialty, Bespoke, and Reinsurance pillars; and Pine Walk, a ‘plug‑and‑play’ MGA platform that launches and scales specialist underwriting teams. TFP underwrites more than 150 lines of business across over 140 countries and is frequently the lead underwriter, helping secure pricing, terms, and conditions for a diversified panel of more than 65 highly rated Capacity Providers. Revenue is primarily derived from placement commissions, with additional profit commissions linked to underwriting performance.

The firm leverages proprietary technology—FireAnt (exposure management and pricing), Prequel (policy administration), Solas (underwriter interface), and Labrador (rules‑based allocation)—to support disciplined selection, real‑time portfolio management, and efficient capacity deployment. Capacity is anchored by a long‑term framework with Pelagos Insurance Capital and by two Lloyd’s syndicates (3123 and 2126), giving TFP access to A/A+ paper, global licensing, and consortium opportunities. TFP emphasizes leadership in complex and dislocated markets, product innovation (e.g., AI data center construction), and targeted growth in high‑potential regions such as Latin America, the Middle East, and Asia.
: Global P&C premiums of about $2.4 trillion in 2024, with commercial lines at roughly $1.1 trillion
: P&C premiums grew ~6% CAGR from 2019 to 2024, with high‑growth regions projected at ~7% annualized through 2036
: Positions itself as the world’s largest independent MGA with multi‑line, global scope
: Large specialty insurers and multi‑line MGAs operating across London, Bermuda, U.S., and E.U. markets
: Shift to delegated underwriting (MGAs), increased alternative capital at Lloyd’s (13% of FAL in 2025), and growing demand in AI, catastrophe‑exposed, and emerging markets
: Serves (re)insureds globally through wholesale, retail, and local brokers; over 10% of premium sourced via direct (re)insured relationships
: Offices in the U.K., Bermuda, Ireland, U.A.E., and the U.S.
: More than 140 countries across Specialty, Bespoke, and Reinsurance pillars
: Over 65 Capacity Providers; 50+ reinsurance partners; 15+ insurance partners via consortia and binding authorities

: 94% lead‑underwriter rate in Fidelis Underwriting; 70% of Bound Premium supported by long‑term capacity; two Lloyd’s syndicates with approved 2026 capacity of ~$1.3 billion; Pine Walk platform at 18 entities with ~170 new‑team prospects in pipeline; typical Pine Walk working‑capital loan ~ $2 million per new entity
, Founder, Chairman & Group CEO - Over 40 years in insurance; previously founded and led Lancashire; established Fidelis Insurance in 2014 and TFP in 2023.
, Deputy Chairman & Group Executive Director - Former Group CRO and Group Director of Underwriting at Fidelis Insurance; prior senior roles at Lancashire.
, Group Chief Financial Officer - Led capacity and corporate finance initiatives including the bifurcation, Lloyd’s platform launches, and term‑loan refinancings.
, Group President – Strategic Partnerships - 25+ years across underwriting and broking; focuses on distribution, partnerships, and broker engagement.
, U.K. Chief Underwriting Officer & Group Head of D&F Property and Energy - Actuarial and underwriting leader with prior roles at AXA XL/Catlin; heads key property and energy lines.
, Group Director of Underwriting - Oversees portfolio strategy and pricing discipline; prior actuarial roles at Brit, Aon, and Allstate.
: Morgan Stanley, Barclays, J.P. Morgan, Deutsche Bank Securities, Dowling & Partners, Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, Citizens Capital Markets, UBS Investment Bank, Natixis
: Repay amounts outstanding under the New Term Loan Facility; remainder for general corporate purposes including working capital, operating expenses, and capex.
